title: A loop that can light

blocks.md:
## A closed path

A lamp lights only when charge can leave the battery, pass through the parts, and return to the battery. That closed path is a series loop. An open gap anywhere on the loop means no current and a dark lamp. Resistance on the loop limits how much current flows. Lower resistance means more current and a brighter lamp — until something overheats.

This bites when you add a lamp but leave a gap, or when you drop resistance to zero to make it brightest. The first case never lights. The second case can push current past a safe cap. In these lessons the current limit is **2**. Brightness without that cap is not a win.

```text
battery → resistor → lamp → battery
```

A common mistake is thinking brightness is the only goal. Safe current is part of the win. This page has no editor: read the loop idea, then go on to the experiment that asks you to brighten a lamp without crossing that cap.
